_doc: Duke Strategies terminology — the BRAND layer. See
clients/_default/voice/terminology.json for what this file is and who reads it.
PROVENANCE (2026-09-08). Derived by measuring, not by guessing: all 21 values
that are byte-identical between src/i18n/content/ui.en.ts and ui.nl.ts on the
live Duke site were read one by one. Every one of them turned out to be
CORRECT Dutch — brand names, or English the Dutch public-affairs register
keeps. So this file is not a list of defects to fix; it is the record that
stops a future translator from 'fixing' them into worse Dutch.
Deliberately NOT recorded: values that are simply the same word in both
languages and carry no decision — Contact, Home, Sitemap, 'Context:',
'Team:', 'Crisis & Media'. A termbase entry should represent a judgement
someone made, not a coincidence of vocabulary.
Dutch general register (workflow, stakeholder, roadmap, …) is inherited from
the nl seed and is not repeated here.
2026-09-17 (ORG-PLAN-276 Phase 2). Four terms added once the site's gate
actually ran them: check-i18n.mjs had imported the termbase loader and
never the checker, so the eight entries above were enforced by nothing for
nine days. Two of the four DEPART from the nl register seed (case study,
crisis management): the seed is a language default and this layer exists to
override it, so a disagreement here is the design working rather than a
conflict to resolve. Every one was verified against the shipped Dutch
before being written; none is aspirational.

nl.rationale: Product name. 'Duke Academie' is the plausible mistake this entry exists to catch.

Duke DEPARTS from the nl register seed here, which says 'case'. The house word is 'Klantcase'/'Klantcases' and the shipped Dutch uses it in all four places it appears (section.caseStudy, whatWeDo.caseStudies, seo.insights.title, seo.insights.desc); src/i18n/glossary.md recorded the choice in prose from the start. 'Casestudie' is academic register and reads wrong on a commercial site, which is the mistake this entry exists to catch.

Duke DEPARTS from the nl register seed here, which closes the compound to 'crisismanagement'. Both are defensible Dutch; Duke's glossary lists it among the industry terms kept in English, and the shipped Dutch keeps it in every one of the six places it appears, including the Crisis Communications service copy. Recorded so the next pass does not close the compound on half of them and leave the other half open — the drift, not the spelling, is what costs.
'Openbaar bestuur' is public ADMINISTRATION — a category error, not a translation. The Dutch sector calls the discipline public affairs, and it is half of what Duke sells.
Standard in the Dutch M&A register. 'Boekenonderzoek' exists and names a narrower, accounting-only activity.
Kept wholesale in the Dutch communications register. 'Opinieleiderschap' is understood but reads as a translation.
Service-line name. 'stakeholder' is kept in Dutch anyway (see the nl register seed); translating only the second half would produce a hybrid.
Job title, used untranslated in Dutch professional-services firms.
Duke's own title for its senior network. A name, not a description.

Common in the Dutch consulting register, but 'op te leveren werk' is also correct and Dutch closes the compound with the loanword as the TAIL, which keep-source cannot enforce. Recorded as 'either' deliberately rather than as a rule that would fail on correct copy.
